The proposed common-audit oracle inequality is false uniformly over \(\mathcal M_n\), even with exact learned images and zero target, audit, and image defects for the benchmark candidate. More precisely, fix \(B>0\), \(\gamma\in(0,1]\), \(\beta\in(0,2]\), and \(\eta=1/4\). Along \(n=3m\) there are genuine two-atom configurations in \(\mathcal M_n\) for which
\[
 \varepsilon_{H,2}=\varepsilon_{A,2}=\alpha_{2,n}=0,
 \qquad
 \widehat h_{k,\lambda}=0
 \quad\text{for every }(k,\lambda)\in\mathcal K\times\Lambda_n,
\]
while
\[
 \|\widehat h-h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2
 =\varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr},2}^2
 =\gamma B^2
\]
for every sample and
\[
 \inf_{k\in\mathcal K,\lambda\in\Lambda_n}
 \left\{\lambda^{\bar\beta}+\frac{s_{k,n}}{\lambda}\right\}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]
Consequently, for every fixed finite value of \(C\), the proposed high-probability inequality fails with probability one for all sufficiently large \(n\). Every random, data-dependent, or oracle-dependent signed linear or affine combination of the already-trained path elements also equals zero. The nonzero collapsed-path failure frontier is exactly \((0,B^2]\), with \(B^2\) attained at \(\gamma=1\) on genuine two-atom support; it is maximal because the source conditions imply \(\|h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}\le B\). Independently of this impossibility, every realization satisfies \(\|\widehat h-h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2\le4B^2\), and the coefficient \(4\) is supremum-sharp over \(\mathcal M_n\).

defs.def:configuration-class: \(\mathcal M_n\) is the class of complete common-audit TRAE configurations \((P,I_{\mathrm{cr}},I_{\mathrm{tr}},I_{\mathrm{va}},\mathcal A_0,(\phi_{kj},J_k,\mathcal H_k,(h_{k\ell})_{\ell\ge1},\widehat g_{kj})_{k\in\mathcal K,1\le j\le d_{H,k}})\) satisfying \(\texttt{ass:iid}\), \(\texttt{ass:three-way-split}\), \(\texttt{ass:bounded-outcome}\), \(\texttt{ass:bounded-bases}\), \(\texttt{ass:finite-candidates}\), \(\texttt{ass:finite-audit}\), \(\texttt{ass:target-origin}\), \(\texttt{ass:target-compact-convex}\), \(\texttt{ass:target-coefficient-radius}\), \(\texttt{ass:image-estimability}\), \(\texttt{ass:pseudotrue-attainment}\), and \(\texttt{ass:dense-enumeration}\). The source conditions are theorem-side regularity conditions, not membership conditions, and no training-coverage, inverse-stability, or oracle-rate property is built into \(\mathcal M_n\).
defs.def:learned-images: For each \(k\in\mathcal K\) and \(1\le j\le d_{H,k}\), fit \(\widehat g_{kj}\) using only \(I_{\mathrm{cr}}\), set \(\alpha_{k,n}=\max_{1\le j\le d_{H,k}}\|\widehat g_{kj}-g_{kj}\|_{L_2(P_Z)}\), and set \(\widehat{\mathcal F}_k=\{\sum_{j\in J_k}u_j\widehat g_{kj}:\sum_{j\in J_k}|u_j|\le B\}\).
defs.def:common-audit: \(\mathcal F^{\mathrm A}=\operatorname{absconv}(\mathcal A_0\cup\bigcup_{k\in\mathcal K}\{\sum_{j\in J_k}u_jg_{kj}:\sum_{j\in J_k}|u_j|\le B\})\), \(\widehat{\mathcal F}^{\mathrm A}=\operatorname{absconv}(\mathcal A_0\cup\bigcup_{k\in\mathcal K}\widehat{\mathcal F}_k)\), \(D_{\mathcal F^{\mathrm A}}(v)=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F^{\mathrm A}}\{2E_P[v(Z)f(Z)]-E_P[f(Z)^2]\}\), \(\varepsilon_{H,k}=\inf_{h\in\mathcal H_k}\|h-h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}\), and \(\varepsilon_{A,k}^2=\sup_{h\in\mathcal H_k}\{\|q_h-q_{h^\dagger}\|_{L_2(P_Z)}^2-D_{\mathcal F^{\mathrm A}}(q_h-q_{h^\dagger})\}_+\).
defs.def:two-atom-constant-configuration: Fix \(B>0\), \(\gamma\in(0,1]\), and put \(a=B\sqrt{\gamma}\). Let \(X=Z\in\{-1,1\}\) with \(P(X=Z=1)=p\in(0,1)\), let \(Y=a\) almost surely, and write \(\mathbf 1\) for the constant-one function. Set \(h_0=w=a\mathbf 1\), \(\mathcal K=\{1,2\}\), \(d_{H,1}=d_{H,2}=1\), \(\phi_{11}=\phi_{21}=\mathbf 1\), \(\mathcal H_1=\{0\}\), and \(\mathcal H_2=\{c\mathbf 1:0\le c\le a\}\). Take \(J_1=\{1\}\), \(J_2=\varnothing\), set \(\widehat g_{11}=\widehat g_{21}=\mathbf 1\) and \(a_{1,n}=a_{2,n}=0\), enumerate \(\mathcal H_1\) by zero and enumerate a countable dense subset of \(\mathcal H_2\) with \(h_{21}=0\), and set \(\mathcal A_0=\{0\}\). Form the learned training critics and common audit by \(\texttt{def:learned-images}\) and \(\texttt{def:common-audit}\). Along \(n=3m\), use any deterministic balanced three-way partition and set \(\eta=1/4\).
defs.def:common-audit-selector: For \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(\lambda\in\Lambda_n\), and \(\ell\ge1\), let \(A_{k,\lambda,\ell}=\sup_{f\in\widehat{\mathcal F}_k}\{2P_{\mathrm{tr}}[(Y-h_{k\ell}(X))f(Z)]-P_{\mathrm{tr}}[f(Z)^2]\}+\lambda P_{\mathrm{tr}}[h_{k\ell}(X)^2]\). Let \(\widehat h_{k,\lambda}\) be the least-index \(h_{k\ell}\) whose score is within \(n^{-1}\) of \(\inf_{m\ge1}A_{k,\lambda,m}\), with index one as a deterministic fallback. Set \(\widehat V_{k,\lambda}=\sup_{f\in\widehat{\mathcal F}^{\mathrm A}}\{2P_{\mathrm{va}}[(Y-\widehat h_{k,\lambda}(X))f(Z)]-P_{\mathrm{va}}[f(Z)^2]\}\), \(\operatorname{pen}_n=8B^2\sqrt{\log(4K|\Lambda_n|/\eta)/n_{\mathrm{va}}}\), and let \((\widehat k,\widehat\lambda)\) be the lexicographically least minimizer of \(\widehat V_{k,\lambda}+\operatorname{pen}_n\); finally set \(\widehat h=\widehat h_{\widehat k,\widehat\lambda}\). The selection stage is restricted to the finite trained path \(\{\widehat h_{k,\lambda}:k\in\mathcal K,\lambda\in\Lambda_n\}\). A path-restricted selector means any measurable map valued in that set, and a convex path aggregation means any convex combination of its elements; neither operation retrains a candidate.
defs.def:training-coverage-defect:
For every \(k\in\mathcal K\), define the bounded training critic body
\[
 \mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{tr}}
 =\left\{\sum_{j\in J_k}u_jg_{kj}:\sum_{j\in J_k}|u_j|\le B\right\}
\]
and
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr},k}^2
 =\sup_{h\in\mathcal H_k}
 \left\{
 \|q_h-q_{h^\dagger}\|_{L_2(P_Z)}^2
 -\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{tr}}}
 \left(2E_P[(q_h-q_{h^\dagger})(Z)f(Z)]-E_P[f(Z)^2]\right)
 \right\}.
\]
Equivalently, as proved in \(\texttt{lem:training-coverage-distance-identity}\),
\[
 \varepsilon_{\mathrm{tr},k}^2
 =\sup_{h\in\mathcal H_k}
 \operatorname{dist}_{L_2(P_Z)}^2
 \bigl(q_h-q_{h^\dagger},\mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{tr}}\bigr).
\]
The inner dual problem is a finite-dimensional concave quadratic optimization over an \(\ell_1\)-ball, and the outer problem is over the compact coefficient set defining \(\mathcal H_k\). The relevant geometry is the compact bounded critic body itself, not merely its linear span.

assumptions.ass:three-way-split: \(I_{\mathrm{cr}},I_{\mathrm{tr}},I_{\mathrm{va}}\) are a deterministic partition of \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with positive cardinalities.
assumptions.ass:target-compact-convex: \(\mathcal H_k\) is a compact convex subset of \(\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{kj}:1\le j\le d_{H,k}\}\) for every \(k\in\mathcal K\).
assumptions.ass:image-estimability: For every \(k\in\mathcal K\) and \(1\le j\le d_{H,k}\), \(g_{kj}\) is \(L_2(P_Z)\)-estimable from \(I_{\mathrm{cr}}\) at deterministic radius \(a_{k,n}\).
assumptions.ass:dense-enumeration: For every \(k\in\mathcal K\), \(\{h_{k\ell}:\ell\ge1\}\subset\mathcal H_k\) is a fixed countable \(L_2(P_X)\)-dense subset containing \(0\).

Suppose a candidate \(k_0\) has \(\varepsilon_{H,k_0}=\varepsilon_{A,k_0}=\alpha_{k_0,n}=0\). If \(0<s_{k_0,n}\le1\) and \(\texttt{ass:grid-coverage}\) holds, then the deterministic grid functional satisfies
\[
 \inf_{\lambda\in\Lambda_n}
 \left\{\lambda^{\bar\beta}+\frac{s_{k_0,n}}{\lambda}\right\}
 \le3s_{k_0,n}^{\bar\beta/(1+\bar\beta)}.
\]
This algebraic optimization does not imply a rate for \(\widehat h\) under \(\mathcal M_n\): \(\texttt{thm:common-audit-oracle-impossibility}\) gives zero-defect configurations for which the displayed functional converges to zero while \(\|\widehat h-h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2=1/32\) almost surely. Independently, that theorem gives the deterministic clipping bound \(\|\widehat h-h^\dagger\|_{L_2(P_X)}^2\le4B^2\). The grid exponent equals \(\beta/(1+\beta)\) for \(\beta\le1\) and saturates at \(1/2\) for \(\beta>1\).
